name: Antigravity CLI
_submit_timing_note: AGY-PASTE-CR-RACE (rc.25, 2026-10-21 audit d7425790): with delay_ms_before_submit 200 and max_submit_resends 3, a bracketed-paste body got its first Enter 200 ms after the paste, before agy had drawn its [Pasted text #1 +N lines] chip, and the remaining two Enters 350 ms apart; the whole budget was spent in ~0.9 s and the task sat unsent in the composer while the coordinator read it as delivered. For bracketed paste, daemon-core send-submit-engine runs with skipEchoGate, firing the first CR after delay_ms_before_submit and then resending every 350 ms while the session remains idle. 700 ms is the only Enter timing measured to submit a paste (AGY-RAW-INGEST note: Enter 700 ms after the chip left idle in 252 ms), and max_submit_resends 6 gives 6 submit-key attempts in total (first at 700 ms, 5 resends 350 ms apart, last at ~2.45 s). BLANK-ENTER-PILEUP worst case: up to 5 stray Enters if the FSM leaves idle >350 ms after a successful submit (was 2); resends fire only while the session stays idle, and the measured leave-idle latency (252 ms) is inside the 350 ms resend gap.
_posix_bracketed_paste_text_note: AGY-RAW-INGEST (2026-10-11, agy 1.3.3 measured through node-pty at 100x32): agy enables bracketed paste itself (ESC[?2004h at startup). A 5,031-char body written raw took 10.3 s to reach the composer on an idle machine (27-72 s for 5-13 KB under load in the live daemon log), which outran the 20 s echo wait and produced blind submit keys and false SUBMIT NOT CONFIRMED verdicts. The same body as ONE bracketed-paste region landed in 18 ms as a `[Pasted text #1 +123 lines]` chip; Enter 700 ms later left idle in 252 ms and the model answered with values taken from the first AND last lines of an 8,740-char body, so the paste is delivered whole. POSIX only; win32 keeps the win32-input-mode path.
_max_submit_resends_note: BLANK-ENTER-PILEUP (2026-10-10, Jupiter live sample): agy's composer accumulates unconsumed submit keys as blank rows rather than absorbing them (unlike claude-cli's queued-input UI) — a 4485-char body took ~29s to echo, well past the old 14-attempt/4.9s horizon, so the blind-fire fallback then sprayed all 14 total submit-key attempts as blank Enter presses (13 blank rows = 14 total attempts - 1 real submit). Capped to 3 total submit-key attempts (1 initial + 2 resends) so a slow-ingesting body costs at most a couple of stray keystrokes instead of over a dozen. Raised to 6 total submit-key attempts (1 initial + 5 resends) on 2026-10-21 (see _submit_timing_note): the body now arrives as one bracketed paste in tens of ms, so the slow raw ingest this cap was sized against no longer applies.
_win32_input_mode_note: AGY-WIN32-NONASCII (2026-10-09, measured live on a win32 node): agy decodes console key events and silently drops every non-letter non-ASCII character delivered as plain UTF-8 through ConPTY (em/en dashes, smart quotes, ellipsis, euro, arrows, check marks, emoji), in both paste and plain writes; claude-cli on the same node keeps them. Sending them as win32-input-mode key records (VK_PACKET) delivers all of them. Ignored off win32; daemons older than this flag ignore it and keep the old behaviour.
_echo_confirm_note: AGY-COMPOSER-SCROLL (2026-10-09, agy 1.3.2 measured at 80x32 through node-pty + ghostty-vt). agy caps its composer height and scrolls a tall body INSIDE the box: the first rows are replaced by a '> ↑ N more lines' marker, so the head of a long task prompt is in neither the viewport nor the scrollback. With the default head_and_tail echo check every long dispatch waited the 20 s blind-fire backstop ('body never confirmed in composer after ~20070ms'). Same shape as kimi; bytes reach agy in order, so a visible tail implies the head arrived.
_sections_note: MEASURED 2026-06-15 against agy 1.0.8 (Gemini 3.1 Pro). The old spec used positional windows: footer=from_bottom:1, modal=from_bottom:24 until:footer, body=from_top:0 until:modal, status=from_bottom:4 until:footer. Real screens proved two failures: (1) modal=from_bottom:24 is content junk — at idle (~11-line screen) it clamps to the whole banner+composer, and after a turn it is the response tail (e.g. 'We smoothly transition to twelve.'), so extract.title.first_line grabbed the wrong line (the echoed prompt '> Run this...') and buttons were polluted -> activeModal came back null. Fix: modal now anchors on its OWN landmark ('Do you want to proceed?' / 'Requesting permission for:') and runs to end-of-screen (no until). (2) body=from_top:0 until:modal starved to 0 lines whenever the screen is short (idle + early generating), so every body braille check was dead. Fix: body is the whole screen. The footer anchor '? for shortcuts' / 'esc to cancel' DID match live and is kept.

_onboarding_fallback_note: AGY-ONBOARDING-RECURRENCE-GUARD (2026-09-01). Live first-run screens are anchored by their measured titles, 'Choose your color scheme:' and 'Terms of Service & Data Use'. Do not use the surrounding 'Welcome to Antigravity CLI!' banner: it also appears on normal ready screens. The patterns are deliberately unanchored because condition matches default to no multiline flag; ^/$ would bind to the entire section, not a screen line. Known onboarding screens route directly to approval from boot/signing_in/busy. Separate timeouts promote a stuck signing_in screen at 60s, or a quiet busy screen with no ready footer or live activity marker at 90s, to approval even if a future vendor wording change defeats the anchors. Both bounds are well below the native-source consume watchdog at 180s. The busy timeout requires five seconds of whole-screen stability and vetoes the ready footer, esc-to-cancel, and the shipping braille activity marker, so normal completion and an active long-running turn keep their existing paths.
_busyidle_fallback_note: BUSY-IDLE-BOUNDED-FALLBACK (AGY-SPEC-BUSY-WEDGE RCA, 2026-07-26). Same wedge family as the codex-cli fix: after a completed turn, a benign repaint inside the cursor_above:4 window keeps resetting the stable clock faster than stable_ms=1500, so the strict all(4) never passes and the session wedges in busy forever (the wake scheduler keeps re-evaluating; the stable leaf is the only blocker). The exact benign ticker string is NOT yet captured, so NO speculative ignore_lines is added. busy→idle is now an `any` of two arms: arm 1 is the ORIGINAL strict guard, byte-equivalent (not approval modal, not footer `esc to cancel`, footer `? for shortcuts`, stable 1500/cursor_above 4) so quiet completions still idle at ~1.5s; arm 2 is a bounded fallback — the same modal/esc-to-cancel vetoes, the same `? for shortcuts` requirement (load-bearing: it is present during generating and approval too, so it is NOT an idle signal on its own), PLUS a veto on the live activity marker reusing the idle→busy braille `Generating|Running|Thinking` regex on the same body section (drift-free), PLUS elapsed_ms:60000 — so with no active marker and no modal, idle commits within 60s of busy entry even if the stable region never settles. Safety invariants: approval modal (also caught by the priority-100 →approval / priority-110 →trust transitions first), footer `esc to cancel`, or a live braille activity marker each veto BOTH arms (no false idle during generation/approval); the fallback never consults transcript signals (final_assistant_present is NOT used). Known conservative gap: a STALE braille line lingering in the viewport scrollback also vetoes arm 2 — that fails safe (stays busy), never false-idle.
_garbled_frame_note: GARBLED-FRAME FALSE BUSY (preview live defect, 2026-09-24, agy on MoltBook, sessions b4eb68e7 / 86ba5a7d / 63387888). ~40-70s after a completed turn agy repainted without any input and the emulated screen was left as a torn frame: rows 0-17 a stale generating frame (transcript tail, a frozen `⡿  Running command...` spinner line, the composer, and an `esc to cancel ... <model>` status row), a lone frozen braille glyph further down, the real idle footer `? for shortcuts` on the last row, and the cursor parked at (0,0). The frozen braille line fired idle→busy, and then BOTH busy→idle arms were structurally dead: arm 1 because a cursor at row 0 makes the cursor_above:4 window unmeasurable (the engine invariant resets its stable clock on every evaluation), arm 2 because the frozen braille line is exactly the known stale-marker veto. Measured: 82 minutes in busy with 2677 focus-in re-primes and zero PTY output; the owner recovered one by typing `/` and deleting it, which made agy repaint a clean frame. Arm 3 is the spec-level backstop for that shape: the same modal / footer `esc to cancel` vetoes and the same `? for shortcuts` footer requirement as arm 2, but instead of vetoing on the braille marker it requires the WHOLE screen to be frozen for 15s (stable_ms without cursor_above), plus elapsed_ms:60000. A live agy spinner repaints several times a second, so a genuinely generating screen cannot satisfy a 15s whole-screen freeze; a frozen marker is by definition not live activity. The daemon engine additionally issues an input-free resize redraw nudge after 45s of PTY silence in a generating state (daemon-core redraw-nudge.ts), which normally repaints the frame and lets arm 1 commit first; arm 3 covers daemons without that nudge.
_background_marker_note: Added 2026-10-18 with the background-task generating hold. The drawer row and footer task counter the busy guards already match, declared once so the engine can BOUND the hold: marker-only (no spinner, output or modal) for 120 s sends one coordinator notice and for 10 min evaluates the screen as if they were absent, so a dev server the worker leaves running cannot pin the session until the 90-minute ceiling. Matched per line; keep in step with the marker alternatives in the busy guards.

Antigravity needs you to sign in

_native_history_note: MUST use the built-in `reader: antigravity-cli`, NOT a declarative `source`. Current antigravity (agy >=1.0) stores each conversation in a per-session SQLite db at conversations/<uuid>.db whose messages live in protobuf `step_payload` BLOBs (step_type 14=user, 15=assistant), while brain/*/.system_generated/logs/transcript.jsonl is written EMPTY (0 bytes). The declarative jsonl/sqlite executor can neither decode the protobuf blobs nor recover from the empty jsonl, so a `source` block here surfaces 0 assistant messages and providerSessionId=null (verified live on win32 2026-07-01). The antigravity-cli reader (native-history/antigravity-cli-transcript.ts, dispatched via resolveAntigravityPath) decodes the .db protobuf and falls back to brain jsonl / .pb, so it must own this read path.
